hypothesis: Add one task-agnostic graph-equivalent traversal calibration pass after the unchanged five corpus-pretraining epochs: expose each usable training graph equally to its original corpus path and one deterministic, distinct randomized-SMILES traversal of the same graph so the published frozen prior assigns comparable likelihood to chemically identical token orders.
method_thesis: Train a task-agnostic autoregressive SMILES model only on the allowed unlabeled corpus, freeze a copy as the prior, and restart a trainable agent for each independent objective session. Generate the first proposals ancestrally, then use returned oracle scores to apply top-fraction prior-regularized likelihood updates to the agent. Whenever the recent reward trajectory shows sustained improvement, run Beam Enumeration on the current agent without calling the oracle: expand its most probable partial token trajectories, convert chemically interpretable partial strings into connected molecular substructures, and retain a small task-local pool of recurrent motifs. Fill subsequent evaluator-announced batches by sampling complete SMILES de novo from the agent and locally rejecting any valid novel sample that lacks every pooled motif; canonicalize and remove already evaluated or within-batch duplicates before submission. The enumerated objects are transient partial token trajectories, not whole candidate molecules, and neither they nor any corpus molecule are scored, ranked, retrieved, or submitted as a finite library. Thus oracle feedback changes both the policy and a dynamic structural gate on fresh generation, concentrating the 290 adaptive calls on chemistry expressed by successful policy updates while the only success criterion remains the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores.

method_tags.acquisition_mechanism: membership in a task-local beam-derived motif pool before oracle submission, with no scoring of the transient internal samples
method_tags.learning_mechanism: offline corpus language-model training plus task-local top-fraction prior-regularized likelihood updates from current oracle feedback
method_tags.proposal_mechanism: dynamic top-probability beam expansion for motif extraction followed by motif-gated rejection sampling of complete de novo SMILES
method_tags.representation: tokenized SMILES plus RDKit-extracted connected substructures from partial token trajectories

activation_observables.measurement: Before calibration, copy the exact state produced by the unchanged fifth Parent epoch. From the held-out split only, construct a fixed preparation-seed-derived panel of up to 512 connected graphs, retaining for each graph one distinct, vocabulary-compatible randomized traversal after at most eight attempts and recording original identity, randomized path, token ids, attempt seed, round-trip canonical identity, and every rejection. On precisely the same retained randomized token paths, compute token-weighted autoregressive NLL under the pre-calibration Parent-equivalent snapshot and the published post-calibration state; also compute original-path NLL under both states and the randomized-minus-original serialization gap. Report per-seed and pooled pre/post randomized-view NLL, its paired change, panel coverage, and serialization-gap change. Activation requires nonzero exactly round-tripping panel coverage, a pooled decrease in randomized-view NLL, and a pooled decrease in the serialization gap rather than an apparent change caused by a different audit panel.

applicability_conditions: A substantial fraction of corpus and held-out graphs must admit a distinct randomized SMILES within the fixed vocabulary and maximum length; long, symmetric, invalid, or vocabulary-incompatible rows fall back to the original path and weaken calibration exposure.

The fixed randomized held-out panel must represent the traversal shift encountered by later graph-equivalent replay; lower NLL on that panel need not transfer to chemically different or genuinely unsupported graphs.
Equal within-graph view averaging is required so graphs with a retained randomized path do not receive more total calibration weight than fallback graphs.

The calibration remains strictly task agnostic and uses only the allowed unlabeled training split, held-out split, preparation seed, RDKit identity checks, and existing vocabulary; no task identity, initial observation, oracle score, or online memory is available.

Downstream benefit is most plausible for this Parent because its retained online learner explicitly consumes randomized graph-equivalent paths against the frozen prior. The result may not transfer to a policy trained and updated only on one canonical serialization.

Reducing serialization-specific NLL does not create new molecular-graph support and can be unhelpful if the remaining benchmark limitation is absent chemistry, stale historical memory, or motif-gate selectivity rather than token-order bias.

The unchanged two-file artifact, BOS/EOS/padding semantics, model dimensions, and vocabulary must continue to instantiate identical frozen-prior and task-local agent copies; the ordinary ancestral completion and unique-valid diagnostics remain safety checks rather than checkpoint selectors.
research_intent.falsifier: The mechanism did not produce its claimed intermediate behavior if any retained calibration or audit view fails exact canonical round-trip identity, if usable graphs receive unequal within-graph view weight, if no distinct compatible randomized held-out views are retained, or if the pooled held-out randomized-view NLL or randomized-minus-original serialization gap fails to decrease from the exact pre-calibration Parent-equivalent snapshot to the published state. A verified NLL-gap contraction with non-improving benchmark score would instead mean the mechanism activated but its proposed downstream utility did not transfer.

research_intent.mechanism: Add one task-agnostic graph-equivalent traversal calibration pass after the unchanged five corpus-pretraining epochs: expose each usable training graph equally to its original corpus path and one deterministic, distinct randomized-SMILES traversal of the same graph so the published frozen prior assigns comparable likelihood to chemically identical token orders.
research_intent.observed_bottleneck: Parent n-a1feb7fbd3ae trains the frozen prior from one stored SMILES path per corpus row, but its formal seed-0 graph-equivalent replay records expose a large serialization penalty before any reward update: the 4,275 non-original randomized paths have aggregate frozen-prior NLL 2.089319398 per predicted token, versus 0.647413426 on the 1,425 exact sampled paths, even though every retained path round-trips to the same source graph. Node n-1e6816bbc389 shows that choosing among the same unaugmented training checkpoints does not remove this behavior: the terminal epoch won on all three preparation seeds, while its pooled ancestral audit still yielded only 656 unique valid molecules in 768 draws. The limiting behavior is therefore serialization-specific corpus teacher forcing, which leaves the order-sensitive frozen prior poorly calibrated on the equivalent traversals consumed by the Parent's retained online graph replay, rather than selection of the wrong existing epoch.
research_intent.revisit_rationale: Cluster c-9956bd4a51 is Knowledge-only from interventions that marginalized randomized SMILES inside online reward replay (n-a1feb7fbd3ae) or an exact surrogate (n-f851988d522a); it did not change or measure the corpus-trained frozen prior. The current Parent stack is materially different from the earlier surrogate case because graph-equivalent augmented-memory replay is now retained and replicated across all three Search Seeds, while its own logs reveal a 3.2-fold frozen-prior NLL penalty on equivalent randomized paths. This experiment is an active-layer prerequisite with a different causal estimand: corpus-only calibration must lower paired held-out randomized-traversal NLL before any online Layer runs, while online replay and surrogate behavior remain frozen. The earlier Knowledge-only score outcomes therefore do not settle whether removing the prior's serialization mismatch helps this Parent.

The online source suffix, including graph-equivalent feedback replay, Beam Enumeration, motif handling, acquisition, duplicate rejection, and oracle interaction, is byte-identical to the Parent and every formal session completed its 300 calls.

Downstream relevance is strongest for this Parent because its retained learner consumes randomized graph-equivalent paths against the frozen prior. The evidence establishes traversal-likelihood calibration, not new molecular-graph support, and does not imply the same utility for canonical-only policies or for objectives limited by absent chemistry, stale memory, or motif-gate selectivity.

The registered randomized-view NLL and gap still decrease decisively, so this is a supported tradeoff rather than a triggered falsifier.

The calibrated ancestral diagnostic remains usable but does not establish preservation of generative support against the copied Parent state on a common sample panel. The three post-calibration 256-draw panels have completion rates 1.0, 0.9921875, and 0.99609375 and unique-valid rates 0.59375, 0.62890625, and 0.671875. These safety checks pass the implementation gate but can neither attribute support changes to calibration nor show that the newly likely traversal orders correspond to additional molecular graphs.

The observed corpus has unusually broad randomized-view compatibility: only 375/743,856 training rows use the fallback. The bounded attempts nevertheless record 5,075 over-length and 1,392 duplicate-original training attempts, plus 22 source graphs that were not connected canonical molecules. Longer, more symmetric, invalid, or vocabulary-incompatible chemistry could cause many more fallbacks and materially weaken the equal-view exposure.

The fixed audit covers 512 retained graphs from each 2,048-row heldout split, stopping once the quota is filled. It directly supports the traversal shift on those 1,536 graphs but does not establish equivalent likelihood contraction on every heldout graph, on unsupported graph chemistry, or on randomized paths with a different generation procedure.

One continued-optimizer calibration pass produces a large aggregate contraction, but the logs do not isolate whether the same effect persists under additional passes, a reset optimizer, another RDKit randomizer, another corpus, or a policy that never consumes graph-equivalent randomized paths online.

applicability_conditions: A substantial fraction of corpus and held-out graphs must admit a distinct randomized SMILES within the fixed vocabulary and maximum length; long, symmetric, invalid, or vocabulary-incompatible rows fall back to the original path and weaken calibration exposure.

The fixed randomized held-out panel must represent the traversal shift encountered by later graph-equivalent replay; lower NLL on that panel need not transfer to chemically different or genuinely unsupported graphs.
Equal within-graph view averaging is required so graphs with a retained randomized path do not receive more total calibration weight than fallback graphs.

The calibration remains strictly task agnostic and uses only the allowed unlabeled training split, held-out split, preparation seed, RDKit identity checks, and existing vocabulary; no task identity, initial observation, oracle score, or online memory is available.

Reducing serialization-specific NLL does not create new molecular-graph support and can be unhelpful if the remaining benchmark limitation is absent chemistry, stale historical memory, or motif-gate selectivity rather than token-order bias.
